Nội dung chi tiết:
1. Do you often walk in your daily life, and where do you usually go for a walk?
2. What are the health benefits of walking regularly?
3. Do you prefer walking alone or walking with friends and family? Why?
title: Topic 1: Walking & Daily Movement
content:
1. Do you often walk in your daily life, and where do you usually go for a walk?
2. What are the health benefits of walking regularly?
3. Do you prefer walking alone or walking with friends and family? Why?

questions.answer: Yes, I am keen on walking in my daily life, and I usually go for a walk in a nearby park in the late afternoon.
questions.example: I usually walk around the park near my house for about 30 minutes at 5:30 PM on weekdays.
questions.q: Do you often walk in your daily life, and where do you usually go for a walk?
questions.reason: It is cheap and convenient, and it allows me to relax my mind and get fresh air after sitting at my desk all day.

questions.answer: Walking regularly brings a lot of benefits to both physical and mental health.
questions.example: Since I started walking every evening three months ago, I sleep much better at night and rarely feel tired in the morning.
questions.q: What are the health benefits of walking regularly?
questions.reason: To be more specific, it helps me keep fit, stay healthy, strengthen my immune system, and feel more energetic. It can also relieve stress and reduce fatigue.

questions.answer: I prefer walking with my family or close friends rather than walking alone.
questions.example: Every Sunday morning, my mom and I walk together around the lake and talk about our plans for the week.
questions.q: Do you prefer walking alone or walking with friends and family? Why?
questions.reason: Because it lets me spend quality time with my loved ones and strengthen bonds within my family, while we openly share our thoughts and daily stories.

hint.reusedSource: Trục Physical health + Trục Mental health + Bộ đề 1 (Alone vs With others)

Nội dung chi tiết:
1. Have you ever visited a zoo, and what animals did you enjoy seeing the most?
2. Do you think visiting the zoo is a good educational activity for children? Why or why not?
3. Are zoos still popular places to visit in your city today?
title: Topic 2: Zoos & Wild Animals
content:
1. Have you ever visited a zoo, and what animals did you enjoy seeing the most?
2. Do you think visiting the zoo is a good educational activity for children? Why or why not?
3. Are zoos still popular places to visit in your city today?

questions.answer: Yes, I have visited the zoo a few times, and I enjoyed seeing elephants and monkeys the most.
questions.example: I visited Saigon Zoo with my cousins two years ago, and we took lots of photos near the elephant area.
questions.q: Have you ever visited a zoo, and what animals did you enjoy seeing the most?
questions.reason: Watching wild animals in real life is interesting and helps me relax my mind and elevate my mood.

questions.answer: Yes, I think going to the zoo is a great educational activity for young children.
questions.example: When my little brother visited the zoo, he learned what giraffes eat and how to care for animals instead of only seeing them in comic books.
questions.q: Do you think visiting the zoo is a good educational activity for children? Why or why not?
questions.reason: It gives them the opportunity to increase knowledge and broaden their horizons about nature, and teaches them why people should be involved in environmental protection.

questions.answer: Yes, zoos are still quite popular in my city, especially for families with young kids.
questions.example: On weekends or public holidays, many parents bring their children to the city zoo for a picnic and a fun day out.
questions.q: Are zoos still popular places to visit in your city today?
questions.reason: It is affordable and gives families a chance to spend quality time together outdoors and enjoy green space away from busy streets.

hint.reusedSource: Trục Broaden knowledge + Bộ đề 1 (Family leisure) + Cụm đa năng (#11)

should be involved in environmental protection

Tiêu đề đề bài: Part 2 - Situation 1: Choosing a Reward Gift for a Child Moving Up a Grade
Nội dung chi tiết:
Situation: Your child has achieved excellent academic results and is moving up to a new grade. You want to reward them with a meaningful gift and are considering three options:
- A laptop or computer (một chiếc máy tính)
- A holiday trip (một chuyến du lịch)
- A motorbike (một chiếc xe máy)

Which option do you think is the best choice and why?
title: Part 2 - Situation 1: Choosing a Reward Gift for a Child Moving Up a Grade
content:
Situation: Your child has achieved excellent academic results and is moving up to a new grade. You want to reward them with a meaningful gift and are considering three options:
- A laptop or computer (một chiếc máy tính)
- A holiday trip (một chuyến du lịch)
- A motorbike (một chiếc xe máy)

Which option do you think is the best choice and why?

chosen.khen1Text: because it is easy to find in local electronics shops, fits my budget, and my child can use it every day at home for their studies.

khen2ARE.answer: A laptop or computer gives my child the opportunity to increase knowledge and learn useful skills for the new grade.
khen2ARE.example: For example, my child can attend online evening classes from home and prepare school slides easily for the new school year.
khen2ARE.reason: They can make the most of new technology to search for study materials, practice English, and finish homework faster.

chosen.khen3Text: a practical and meaningful reward that reminds my child of my care and encouragement for many years to come.

rejected.reason: riding a motorbike on busy roads is dangerous for a school child, especially when it rains heavily or traffic is crowded, and a young student may not even be old enough for a license.
spending a lot of money on a short holiday trip is inconvenient because the trip ends after a few days, and my child cannot use it for daily study in the new grade.

reusedVocab: gives ... the opportunity to increase knowledge
make the most of new technology
meaningful keepsake / reward that reminds ... of my care
riding motorbikes ... is dangerous, especially when it rains heavily
hint.situation: My child has achieved excellent academic results and is moving up to a new grade. I want to reward them with a meaningful gift and am considering three options: a laptop or computer, a holiday trip, and a motorbike.

title: Part 3 - Topic 1: The Importance of Good Relationships at the Workplace
content:
Topic: The importance of maintaining positive relationships at the workplace
Suggestions:
- Enhancing teamwork and daily work efficiency
- Reducing workplace stress and boosting job satisfaction
- Expanding professional support and career growth opportunities
- [Your own ideas]

Follow-up questions:
1. What qualities help an employee get along well with their colleagues?
2. How should coworkers resolve disagreements or conflicts in the office?
3. What can managers do to build a friendly and collaborative working environment?

hint.coreTopic: the importance of maintaining positive relationships at the workplace

followUps.answer: There are some good qualities that help an employee get along well with colleagues, such as honesty, patience, and a willingness to listen.
followUps.example: For example, an employee who helps a new teammate learn office software quickly earns everyone's trust and respect.
followUps.q: What qualities help an employee get along well with their colleagues?
followUps.reason: Being polite and helpful builds a strong sense of belonging and helps coworkers truly understand each other through face-to-face interaction.

followUps.answer: I think coworkers should stay calm, talk face-to-face privately, and listen to each other to solve the problem.
followUps.example: For instance, if two colleagues disagree on a sales plan, they can sit in a meeting room for 15 minutes and combine the best ideas from both sides.
followUps.q: How should coworkers resolve disagreements or conflicts in the office?
followUps.reason: Thinking things through calmly avoids unnecessary trouble and prevents small work disagreements from turning into personal anger.

followUps.answer: I think managers should support open communication, treat everyone fairly, and organize regular team activities.
followUps.example: For example, a manager can hold a short coffee break every Friday afternoon so team members can relax and talk freely.
followUps.q: What can managers do to build a friendly and collaborative working environment?
followUps.reason: When leaders listen to staff and encourage teamwork, workers feel respected, reduce fatigue, and stay motivated at the office.

mindmapPoints.cue: Enhancing teamwork and daily work efficiency
mindmapPoints.expand: because coworkers share ideas openly and help each other solve problems faster instead of working alone.
mindmapPoints.impact: Therefore, it is good for team productivity and company success.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Good workplace relationships help employees improve teamwork and daily work efficiency.

mindmapPoints.cue: Reducing workplace stress and boosting job satisfaction
mindmapPoints.expand: For example, having friendly colleagues to chat with during lunch breaks helps you put your feet up and elevate your mood on busy days.
mindmapPoints.impact: Clearly, it is beneficial to employees' mental health.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Positive relationships at work help staff relieve stress and feel happier with their job.

mindmapPoints.cue: Expanding professional support and career growth opportunities
mindmapPoints.expand: This is because experienced colleagues and managers are willing to teach you new skills and recommend you for higher positions.
mindmapPoints.impact: So, it has positive effects on your long-term career and living standard.
mindmapPoints.sentence: Good relationships help workers gain professional support and better career opportunities.

hint.ownIdea: I think that 3 ideas are comprehensive. I cannot think of other ideas.
reusedVocab: build a strong sense of belonging and help us truly understand each other through face-to-face interaction
think things through calmly to avoid unnecessary trouble
